chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:

The Faqih, peace be upon him, said: Shortening in salat is at two barids, or one barid going and returning. A barid is six miles, and that is two farsakhs. Shortening applies in four farsakhs. So when a man leaves his home intending twelve miles, and that is four farsakhs, then he reaches two farsakhs while intending to return, or [to continue] another two farsakhs, he shortens. But if he turns back from what he had intended upon reaching two farsakhs and wishes to stay, then full salat is upon him. And if he had shortened and then turned back from his intention, he repeats the salat.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening the four-unit salat during travel
key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the prayer in its full form
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: staying or remaining in place rather than continuing travel
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: a travel measure equal here to six miles
key_terms.فَرْسَخَانِ: two farsakhs, a stated travel distance unit
key_terms.نِيَّتُهُ: his intended purpose or travel intention

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler shorten salat, and what if he changes his intention during the journey?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal threshold for shortening salat during travel and defines the relevant travel measures in miles, barids, and farsakhs. It also clarifies that the ruling depends on the traveler's intention: if he changes his mind and decides to stay after reaching part of the distance, he must perform full salat, and if he had already shortened, he must repeat it.
